overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not announcing the names of remotely participating members at its fully remote June 22 meeting; the policy and muting claims were not OML matters, and the Board was ordered to comply going forward.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to announce at the start of its June 22 fully remote meeting the names of members participating remotely.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law regulations nonetheless require such an announcement.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board and its chair violated the Board's own policies by not letting members speak and muting them during the June 22 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Division does not review for compliance with a public body’s own policies and procedures.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that the chair muting board members during the June 22 meeting violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, this allegation, even if true, would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, including the requirement that the chair announce the names of members participating remotely at the start of meetings.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and note that future similar violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
